daily.summary: Explore the three pillars of Indian sovereignty - border security, civilizational identity and economic independence and how national security, cultural cohesion and self-reliance shape India's future. daily.title: Who Must File Form PAS-6 in India? Share Capital Reconciliation and Filing Deadline
daily.summary: India's Ministry of Corporate Affairs Form PAS-6 requires applicable unlisted public and non-small private companies to reconcile issued capital with demat and physical shares. Companies required to hold their securities in dematerialised form must ensure that their issued share capital reconciles accurately with the securities held in demat and physical form. India’s Union Ministry of Corporate Affair’s (MCA) Form PAS-6 supports this through a half-yearly reconciliation of share capital with the records of depositories and the registrar and transfer agent (RTA). For FY 2026-27, the half-year ended 30 September, and the form is due by 29 November 2026.

daily.title: ITAT Delhi Deletes ₹1.59 Crore Section 57 Disallowance on Tax-Neutral Reclassification
daily.summary: ITAT Delhi deletes ₹1.59 crore addition where interest expenditure was added back under business income and deducted under other sources. C.E. Info Systems Limited earned interest income of ₹15,98,10,859 , which was included in its profit and loss account. For income-tax purposes, the company excluded the gross interest from its business income computation and offered it separately under “ Income from Other Sources .” At the same time, it added back ₹1,59,81,086 to business income, representing expenditure allocated to earning the interest. It then deducted the same amount from the interest income under section 57(iii) .
